title: Mode Transitions and Model Management
description: The TDPO learns when and how to transition between DP modes cleanly, understanding what each transition does to the mathematical model. Professional standard means the TDPO can execute any mode transition smoothly, explain the model implications of each transition, and never select DP onto a vessel with significant residual velocity.

tasks.title: Clean Mode Transition — JSMH to Monitor to DP
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP at datum. Moderate environment settled. Note current vector value before starting.
tasks.execute: Three runs. Each run: select JSMH with zero inputs and allow vessel to drift for 2 minutes. Then slow to near zero. Select Monitor briefly. Select DP. Record capture quality. Vary the vessel speed at the Monitor transition between runs — Run 1 transition at 0.3kts, Run 2 at 0.1kts, Run 3 at near zero. Compare capture quality across all three runs.
professional_standard: Cleanest capture when vessel nearest zero at Monitor transition
Correct explanation of what Monitor does to the model
Improvement in capture quality from Run 1 to Run 3
Time to stable position reducing each run

fields_per_run.label: DP capture quality — smooth or hunting?
Time to stable position after DP selected (seconds)
Current vector value at moment of DP selection

debrief_questions: Why did DP capture quality improve when the vessel was closer to zero speed at the Monitor transition?
What does Monitor actually do to the DP mathematical model — is it a hard reset or something else?
How long did Monitor need to be active before DP capture improved — what does this tell you about the model?
When would you use this JSMH to Monitor to DP sequence in a real operational scenario?

variants.title: Transition After Large Transit
variants.note_to_tdpo: Complete a 500m JSMH transit first, then apply the clean transition technique. This simulates moving between work locations. Model corruption will be greater — observe how this affects the required Monitor duration.

tasks.title: Minimum Power Mode Observation
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP holding a fixed heading. Record current heading and total thruster demand as baseline.
tasks.execute: Select Minimum Power mode. Observe as the vessel weathervanes toward the minimum resistance heading. Record what heading it settles on. Compare this to the minimum power heading you found manually in env_002 — do they agree? Hold the settled heading for 10 minutes and record demand reduction achieved compared to the fixed heading baseline.
professional_standard: Correctly observe and record weathervane behaviour
Compare settled heading to env_002 result
Understand operational limitations of this mode

variants.title: Minimum Power in Changing Conditions
variants.note_to_tdpo: Your DPO will change the wind direction mid-task. Observe whether the vessel re-weathervanes. How quickly does it respond? What are the implications if this happens during an operation?

tasks.title: JSAH vs JSMH Comparison
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP at datum. Moderate conditions settled.
tasks.execute: Part 1 — Surge move in JSMH: Select JSMH and make a controlled 100m surge move North. Record heading drift during the move. Return to datum. Part 2 — Same surge move in JSAH: Select JSAH and repeat the identical move. Record heading drift. Compare. Part 3 — Heading change in each mode: Attempt a 20 degree heading change in JSMH, then in JSAH. Compare the experience and result.
professional_standard: Correctly identify heading behaviour difference between modes
Articulate when each mode is appropriate
Complete all three parts with observations recorded
Correct statement of fundamental difference between modes
